messages:
sre_pager: paging oncall — multiple customer reports of generation corruption and 5xx spikes from hosted inference (gpu-pool-3). alerts: error-rate up ~7.8% over last 10m, tail latency spiking, memory on a subset of inference nodes growing steadily. tagging oncall: @alice

alice (oncall): seeing same. graph: kv-cache size for model-rs-7b jumped from ~200MB to ~2.1GB on several pods. continuous-batching queue depth doubled. any recent rollouts?

ben (eng-runtime): we pushed a batching tweak to reduce latency ~30m ago (autoscale/packets: continuous-batching enabled, max_batch_tokens lowered). not aware of cache change. I can pull logs.

dinesh (serving): I'm seeing repeated log pattern: "kvcache: reuse entry mismatch, seq_offset 0 != expected 1024" across multiple requests. appears to correlate with paged attention path.

elaine (support): two paying customers filing issues: AcmeHealth (prod) and NoteStream (beta). AcmeHealth reports garbled outputs and aborted requests. escalating.

alice (oncall): first mitigation: throttle continuous batching for gpu-pool-3 and enable strict per-request context checks. applying hotfix now.

alice (oncall): runbook step — reduce batch window to 0 and set batching.max_batch_size=1 for pool selector gpu-pool-3:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://infra.internal/api/pools/gpu-pool-3/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"batching": {"mode": "sync", "max_batch_size": 1, "batch_window_ms": 0}}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy accepted. job id: deploy-9927. rolling to 6/6 nodes.

ops-bot: kvcache flush initiated with selector=pool=gpu-pool-3 by alice. command: `rbxctl kvcache flush --selector "pool=gpu-pool-3" --parallel 12`

alice (oncall): flush completed on 5/6 nodes, one failed (OOM on pod-12). requeued flush for pod-12.

ben (eng-runtime): looking at request traces: when requests are paged (long sequences) and continuous batching merges contexts, we sometimes carry old KV entries without validating "context_id" and "seq_offset". the batching change likely increased reuse window so stale kv entries were reused across requests that shouldn't share them.

dinesh (serving): reproducer gist:
```python
# simplified repro: two concurrent requests A,B with different seq start offsets
# continuous batch groups them -> one KV cache slot used for both
# missing per-request seq_offset check leads to stale tokens appended
```

elaine (support): AcmeHealth confirms outputs stabilizing after~10m post-flush but wants incident timeline and mitigation notes. ETA for full fix?

alice (oncall): error rate dropped from 7.8% -> 1.4% after throttling + flush. tail latency improving. filing customer notifications.

carla (pm): schedule postmortem, please include impact list (tenants + request ids), timeline, root cause, and remediation plan. I'll coordinate customer comms for AcmeHealth and NoteStream.

ben (eng-runtime): proposed short-term fix (merge into urgent branch): add strict seq_offset validation at cache lookup and drop entries if ctx_id mismatch; also add a fast-path that disables cross-request reuse when request metadata indicates paged attention. prepping PR.

ben (eng-runtime): PR: https://git.internal/rw/serving/pull/4382 (WIP) — includes tests for cross-request kv hits and a new circuit to disable reuse in paged mode.

deploy-bot: canary deploy of pr-4382 to gpu-pool-canary started (2 nodes).

alice (oncall): handoff to ben at 22:10 UTC — I'm logging off in 30m but will be reachable for escalation. summary: throttled continuous batching on affected pool, flushed kvcache, canary deploy running.

ben (eng-runtime): canary looks clean for 12m. no kvcache reuse errors in logs. rolling to remaining nodes with staged ramp: 3 nodes every 5m.

dinesh (serving): note: added metric `kvcache.validation.skip_ratio` to monitor how often entries are dropped due to seq/context mismatch. watching for regressions.

ops-bot: rollout complete to gpu-pool-3. all 6/6 nodes on pr-4382.

alice (oncall): support update sent. AcmeHealth assigned escalation priority P1 -> downgraded to P3 based on stabilization but keep them on watch.

carla (pm): assign authors for postmortem: ben (cause + code), dinesh (repro + tests), alice (ops timeline), carla (customer comms). deadline: EOD tomorrow.

ben (eng-runtime): permanent mitigation items: 1) add end-to-end KV cache invariants in CI (ctx_id, seq_offset, model_version), 2) telemetry for batch composition (how many distinct contexts are batched together), 3) opt-in canary for future batching changes.

dinesh (serving): long-term idea: namespace KV slots by request-scoped UUID and garbage collect; more memory but safer. putting notes in the design doc.

elaine (support): posting customer note draft for AcmeHealth. pinging legal for SLA implications.

alice (oncall): closing incident thread for now, leaving follow-ups in #postmortems link (postmortem ticket created: PMT-3119). thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sre_pager: incident resolved — please file postmortem and link here when ready.
